extracted.intended_audience: business leaders, industrial managers, entrepreneurs, and students of industrial organization
extracted.subtask_description: Practical business-management and organizational principles for running 19th-century mills and steelworks, including hiring, promotion, partnership terms, vertical integration, accounting, and personal conduct (public speaking, writing, travel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote those who render exceptional service
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no way of making a business successful that can vie with the policy of promoting those who render exceptional service."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal promotion as a primary tool for building a successful organization. Examples: William Borntraeger rose from shipping clerk to partner and sizeable income through zeal and industry; William L. Abbott and Mr. Curry likewise advanced from modest positions to partnership and leadership. Promotion rewards merit and creates loyalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dual authority in the same works
rubrics_metrics.description: "Upon no account could two men be in the same works with equal authority. An army with two commanders-in-chief, a ship with two captains, could not fare more disastrously than a manufacturing concern with two men in command upon the same ground..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When organizing departments that share the same physical works, designate one person as captain with sole authority and have them report to a single superior. Carnegie credits this decision (choosing Mr. Jones as 'The Captain') as decisive for success at Edgar Thomson Works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire managers with appropriate manufacturing experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Office skill does not automatically translate to manufacturing ability: an excellent auditor could not be expected 'to step into manufacturing and be successful from the start. He had neither the knowledge nor the training for this new work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match job duties to prior experience and training. Recognize that great office/accounting talent may still be unsuitable for hands-on manufacturing leadership; avoid placing purely administrative people into critical production roles without retraining or proper support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Own raw materials and finish the completed article (vertical integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The one vital lesson in iron and steel that I learned in Britain was the necessity for owning raw materials and finishing the completed article ready for its purpose."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate backward (e.g., build blast furnaces) to secure supply and control cost/quality. Carnegie describes building furnaces and later acquiring mines and producing ferro-manganese domestically, reducing dependence on foreign suppliers and cutting prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate acquisitions thoroughly before purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: Before buying a mine or plant, conduct a thorough investigation to prove there is enough resource/value to repay the investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Phipps obtained an option and only after a careful investigation did the firm acquire a Virginia manganese mine. Conversely, warning: purchasing inferior plants is 'unsatisfactory' (Escanaba Furnace purchase cost as much as a new one and was inferior), though such mistakes can occasionally yield unexpected benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision in accounting and use clerks to check transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: "So perfect was our system of accounts that we knew the exact amount of the profit... There is nothing more profitable than clerks to check up each transfer of material from one department to another in process of manufacture."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain detailed, department-to-department accounting to know true margins. Employ clerks to audit material transfers and internal movements to prevent loss, reveal true costs, and enable accurate profit measurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure partnership interests to limit immediate financial burden
rubrics_metrics.description: When giving partners an interest, arrange that 'the cost of the interest given was payable only out of profits.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting interests payable only from future profits reduces immediate financial exposure of the firm and allows promotion without requiring partners to meet capital calls; used when admitting young employees as partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward and care for key employees (travel, salary, recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give deserving employees opportunities and rewards (trips, promotion, fair salary) rather than expecting them to carry burdens without recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: William Borntraeger was given a trip to Europe after overwork; Captain Jones preferred a high salary to partnership because he did not want 'his thoughts running on business.' Such gestures maintain morale and retain talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't expect competitors to immediately recognize new entrants; be proactive in securing orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitors may ignore a new firm; proactively obtain orders to establish market presence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Competitors initially ignored Carnegie's new steelworks, so the firm sent agents to take orders at best prices and secured enough orders to justify starting operations. Active market development is required rather than passive expectation of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value zeal, industry, and hands-on knowledge in employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical qualities such as unflagging zeal, industry, intimate knowledge of the mill, and willingness to be everywhere about the works are central to employee value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carnegie's account of Borntraeger's rise emphasizes eagerness to learn (learned English), constant presence, and practical awareness as decisive traits for promotion and profitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be your natural self in public speaking; avoid affected elocution
rubrics_metrics.description: For youthful orators: 'When you stand up before an audience reflect that there are before you only men and women... Be your own natural self and go ahead.' Colonel Ingersoll: 'Avoid elocutionists like snakes,' and 'be yourself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speak conversationally as if talking to people you know; authenticity beats artificial mannerisms. This is practical public-speaking advice for speakers addressing general audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write honestly and without forced effort; write for friends first
rubrics_metrics.description: "The writer of a book designed for his friends has no reason to anticipate an unkind reception... I wrote for my friends; and what one does easily, one does well."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose with natural ease and personal honesty rather than calculated attempts to impress. Carnegie's own privately circulated travel notes later became published works; writing without forced effort can resonate with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that mistakes can have secondary benefits but are still avoidable
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchases of inferior plants are 'unsatisfactory' and often a mistake, yet such mistakes 'proved... a source of great profit' later by enabling new products (e.g., spiegel, ferro-manganese).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While avoidable errors (buying inferior plants) should be minimized via due diligence, be open to repurposing assets and finding unexpected value in imperfect acquisitions.
